narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 39% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reason the model is concerned is that you’ve said you don’t plan to pursue higher education after high school. Almost all students who aren’t required to take remedial courses have expressed a clear goal of going to university, so this difference stands out. While it doesn’t mean you’re certain to fail, it does suggest you may lack motivation or a long-term plan, which can affect your effort and focus in class.

On a more positive note, you’ve chosen this school because of its strong reputation, which the model sees as a sign you care about your education. You also haven’t failed any classes in the past, which is another encouraging factor. These two points help balance the prediction, but they aren’t enough to outweigh the concern about your future plans.

The remedial courses will give you structured time to catch up on any gaps, build consistent study habits, and clarify your goals. Since you’re only 16 and still have time to explore your options, this is a good opportunity to reflect on what you want after graduation. Use this support to stay engaged, ask questions, and take small steps toward a plan that excites you—whether that’s further education, training, or work. The extra help is here to make sure you finish strong.
